title: Quest's --if-revision narrows to per-record (QCLI-310), making lore-cli's workspace-wide revision comment and the race test's positive control stale
description:
Filed on opum-agent's cross-session notice, 2026-09-29, and verified here against HEAD d19ce1c8 rather than taken on the relay. opum-ai/quest-cli#415 (QCLI-310, not yet merged or released) narrows Quest's --if-revision from workspace-wide to per-record. No behaviour lore depends on changes -- LCLI-614 SF1 already declines to decide on revision movement alone, and a narrower hash strengthens that -- but two artifacts in this repository assert the old behaviour and one of them goes red once a Quest carrying the fix is installed.

(1) src/commands/link.ts:610-611 states, present tense: "Quest's revision is WORKSPACE-WIDE (measured on 0.10.0 and 0.11.0 -- editing T-1 changes T-2's viewed revision)". That measurement stays true of the versions it names; the comment is stale as a claim about Quest's contract, not wrong about its own measurement.

(2) test/link-quest-race.test.ts:231 is the POSITIVE CONTROL for the competing-removal race: expect(after).not.toBe(revisions[0]) -- it asserts that T-1's viewed revision MOVES under a T-2 write. Under per-record revisions that assertion fails, which is the control doing its job rather than a defect in the test.

Both move together when the release lands, and neither should move before it: changing the comment early would misdescribe the installed Quest, and retargeting the control early would stop it proving anything. The controlling fact is the release, and the narrowing is to be confirmed by MEASUREMENT against the released binary (edit one task, view another) -- never by reading a version number or a changelog.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The narrowed behaviour is confirmed by measurement against the released Quest binary -- editing one task and viewing another shows a revision that does NOT move -- and the measurement is recorded on this task before either artifact is changed

src/commands/link.ts no longer states that Quest revision is workspace-wide as present-tense contract, and the correction names the Quest release that narrowed it and cites the measurement rather than a version comparison

test/link-quest-race.test.ts:231 no longer asserts that T-1's viewed revision moves under a T-2 write: the positive control is retargeted or inverted to a property that still distinguishes a guarded edit from an unguarded one
bun test and bun run lore check exit 0

implementationNotes:
AC1 MEASUREMENT, 2026-09-30, by the lore-cli session, against the RELEASED quest 0.12.0 (the workstation's global `quest --version` reads 0.12.0): `bun test test/link-quest-race.test.ts` fails its third case exactly as this task predicts — `expect(after).not.toBe(revisions[0])` at test/link-quest-race.test.ts:231, with `Expected: not "c54ff5466ccb8b0f35239cc003ce30145f7873be21f789c31078c3b12e61700f"` — i.e. T-1's viewed revision did NOT move under the T-2 write. That is AC1's measurement: editing one task and viewing another shows a revision that does not move, on the released binary, recorded before either artifact is changed.

Two notes for whoever works this. The file skips itself in CI (Bun.which("quest") is null in the lint/typecheck/test job, which installs no quest), so this red is workstation-only and has been invisible to every CI run. And the same session measured that this workstation's global quest is 0.12.0 — the pair-lock trap on LCLI-621 describing it as 0.11.0 is stale.

AC1 RE-MEASURED, 2026-10-06, by the lore-cli session, against the RELEASED quest 0.12.0 (workstation `quest --version` reads 0.12.0), in a throwaway quest workspace under the session scratchpad: created T-1 and T-2, captured both revisions, ran `quest task edit T-1 --add-label bump --actor ... --actor-kind human`, then re-viewed both. Result: editing T-1 MOVED T-1's own revision (YES) and did NOT move T-2's viewed revision (NO). So the per-record narrowing is confirmed by MEASUREMENT against the released binary, not by a version number or a changelog. This reproduces the 2026-09-30 note's finding independently. Implementing AC2 (the src/commands/link.ts comment) and AC3 (the race test's positive control) against this.
